returnedItinerary.intro: Five days including flight arrival and return: three nights in Springdale followed by one in Bryce Canyon City, with only one hotel change. narrativeSections.heading: Access and seasonal checks
narrativeSections.markdown:
This undated plan does not assume trails or roads are open. Check conditions before travel, especially Lower Emerald Pool's direct access; if unavailable, replace that morning with a flexible easy outing advised by park staff rather than a longer detour. Snow or ice can make Bryce's rim walks unsuitable, while summer heat calls for shorter, earlier walks and more rest. Stay off affected trails during storms or flood warnings.

During Zion's shuttle season, private vehicles cannot use Zion Canyon Scenic Drive; use the [official shuttle schedule](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/zion-canyon-shuttle-system.htm) for your dates. Bryce's [seasonal shuttle](https://www.nps.gov/brca/planyourvisit/shuttle.htm) is optional and can simplify parking. Road travel times and hotel availability have not been confirmed. Utah is generally one hour ahead of Las Vegas; check local clocks for your travel dates.

returnedItinerary.intro: Three full September sightseeing days based in West Yellowstone, prioritizing wildlife, geysers and scenic viewpoints with short walks and no difficult hikes. Assumes a vehicle for sightseeing, not arrival or departure days. Lamar Valley is deliberately the longest travel day; the canyon day afterward allows a slower afternoon. Walking distances below are approximate, not mandatory targets; turn back earlier when needed.

days.label: Geysers and colorful hot springs

stops.name: Old Faithful
stops.note: Allow time to wait for an eruption and sit at the viewing area. Check the posted prediction on arrival; keep any additional boardwalk exploration short rather than attempting the whole Upper Geyser Basin.

stops.name: Grand Prismatic Spring
stops.note: Use the Midway Geyser Basin boardwalk, roughly 0.8 mile for the full circuit, only if comfortable. This is a ground-level view, not the elevated overlook hike; steam can obscure colors on cold mornings.

stops.name: Fountain Paint Pot
stops.note: A roughly half-mile boardwalk circuit adds bubbling mud and varied thermal features. Some slopes and steps may be tiring; skip this final stop if the earlier walking has been enough.

dayStructure.summary: A focused geyser-basin day, allowing eruption waiting time and breaks between short boardwalk outings.

blocks.label: Watch Old Faithful erupt
blocks.note: Approach from West Yellowstone with a generous traffic buffer, then settle into the main geyser experience.

blocks.label: Lunch and a seated break
blocks.note: Bring a picnic or use available services before heading north through the geyser corridor.

blocks.label: See the colors of Grand Prismatic
blocks.note: This is the main afternoon walk, with the pace set by your parents.

blocks.label: Explore bubbling mud pots
blocks.note: Make this a short final outing on the return toward your base.

blocks.label: Dinner and rest in West Yellowstone
blocks.note: Return to your base and prepare binoculars, layers and picnic food for the wildlife day.

days.label: Lamar Valley wildlife safari

stops.name: Lamar Valley
stops.note: Watch from designated roadside pullouts using binoculars or a spotting scope. Spend time scanning rather than hiking; bison are a central attraction, while bear and wolf sightings are uncertain. Move between pullouts only when parking is safe.

dayStructure.summary: A wildlife-first day with a long approach, extended roadside watching and no added sightseeing checklist.

blocks.label: Early drive from West Yellowstone to Lamar Valley
blocks.note: Leave early for the long cross-park approach; allow several hours and extra time for wildlife traffic. Avoid a rigid dawn-arrival target and drive cautiously in low light.

blocks.label: Scan Lamar Valley for wildlife
blocks.note: Keep the day centered on patient wildlife watching with minimal walking.

blocks.label: Picnic and a proper break
blocks.note: Bring lunch so you are not dependent on distant or seasonal food services; eat away from wildlife and secure all food.

blocks.label: Return from Lamar Valley to West Yellowstone
blocks.note: Allow a generous afternoon for the return rather than adding Mammoth or other distant attractions; aim to finish the long drive before dark.

blocks.label: Quiet evening at your base
blocks.note: Have dinner and rest after the trip's most driving-intensive day.

days.label: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone viewpoints

stops.name: Artist Point
stops.note: Take the short approach from parking for the classic canyon and Lower Falls panorama. Use the first comfortable viewing area rather than extending onto rim trails or taking extra stairs.

stops.name: Lookout Point
stops.note: Visit the upper viewpoint for a contrasting Lower Falls perspective. Do not descend the steep Red Rock Trail; use only the short viewpoint approach and skip it if the slope feels uncomfortable.

dayStructure.summary: Two complementary canyon views, followed by an unhurried lunch and recovery time rather than a demanding hike.

blocks.label: Enjoy the canyon panorama at Artist Point
blocks.note: Allow a leisurely approach from West Yellowstone and make this the day's main scenic experience.

blocks.label: See the falls from the opposite rim
blocks.note: Drive between the canyon rims for a second perspective without a connecting hike.

blocks.label: Unhurried lunch near Canyon
blocks.note: Take a seated break; a packed lunch keeps plans flexible if seasonal services are limited.

blocks.label: Return and relax in West Yellowstone
blocks.note: Leave room for the cross-park return, then enjoy a genuinely free afternoon at your base rather than adding more walking.

blocks.label: Final sightseeing-day dinner
blocks.note: Finish with dinner in West Yellowstone; no departure logistics are assumed.

narrativeSections.heading: Before you go
narrativeSections.markdown: Confirm roads, boardwalk access, weather and seasonal services for your September dates using [Yellowstone's official planning information](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/index.htm). Specific access has not been confirmed for your travel dates; if a stop is unavailable, shorten that day's outing rather than substituting a strenuous trail. Yellowstone generally requires a vehicle or organized tour for these distances, not reliance on a park-wide public shuttle. Bring warm layers, binoculars, water and picnic food. Stay on thermal boardwalks; keep at least 100 yards from bears and wolves and 25 yards from other wildlife. September elk can be particularly aggressive during the rut.

blocks.note: Return to Port Angeles when ready, relax, and pack for tomorrow's single lodging move.

days.label: Move west and explore Rialto Beach

stops.name: Rialto Beach
stops.note: A short approach reaches a pebble beach with ocean views. Wander as far as feels comfortable; the longer walk to Hole in the Wall is not part of this relaxed outing. Stay clear of surf and unstable driftwood.

blocks.label: Move from Port Angeles to Forks
blocks.note: Check out and travel west with time for breaks; arrange luggage storage if your room is not ready.

blocks.label: Lunch in Forks
blocks.note: Eat before heading to the beach and pick up any picnic supplies.

blocks.label: Settle into the western base

days.label: An immersive Hoh Rain Forest morning

stops.name: Hoh Rain Forest
stops.note: Explore the developed rainforest area at an unhurried pace, choosing short forest walks rather than committing to a long backcountry hike. Bring water, lunch, and a light rain layer.

days.label: Ruby Beach and a gentle coastal finale

stops.name: Ruby Beach
stops.note: Follow the short coastal-forest approach to views of sea stacks and the beach. Expect uneven footing near the shore. Tidepool only when tides and sea conditions permit, staying well back from breaking waves.

narrativeSections.heading: Before you go
narrativeSections.markdown: August is typically busy; arrange lodging ahead and carry layers for cool, foggy coastlines and cooler mountain weather. Check [Olympic's official planning pages](https://www.nps.gov/olym/planyourvisit/directions.htm) for travel-date road access, transport or shuttle arrangements, entry requirements, and trail conditions; these are not confirmed for your undated August trip. Keep Hurricane Ridge on the clearest feasible day by swapping the first two days if useful. If mountain or rainforest access is disrupted, retain that day's relaxed pace and choose an accessible local alternative rather than attempting a long detour. At the coast, check tides and marine conditions and avoid headland crossings on these casual outings.
